metrics.noLagSamples: No lag samples. Either no consumer group is committing offsets on this topic, or the lag sampler could not reach the broker — check the run log.

run.title: Run
run.noRun: No run selected. Pick a profile and press Start.
run.scenariosHint: Where the load went. Artillery reports only a virtual-user count per scenario; k6 tags every request, so its rows also carry the scenario's own requests, success rate and p95.
run.lagGrowthHint: Above 0: consumers fell behind while the load ran — the backlog grows without bound at this rate.
run.lagNone: No consumer group committed offsets on this topic, so there is no lag to summarise.
run.closeTab: Close this tab (the run keeps going)
run.runsConcurrently: Selected profiles all start at once and share this machine — their latency figures do affect each other.
run.errorBodyEmpty: The target replied with an empty body.
run.msgLagUntracked: {{count}} message(s) were not tracked (acks=0 returns no offset, or the tracking cap was reached).
run.msgLagHint: Every acked message is timed from produce until the group's committed offset is seen past it. Resolution is the 1 s lag sample plus the group's commit interval (auto-commit is 5 s by default). Pending = never consumed before the run ended — set a drain wait to let the tail finish.
run.monitorWaiting: Waiting for the first lag sample… A shared cluster can take a few seconds per sample — the run log says so if it does.

capacity.title: Capacity (ramp) analysis
capacity.hint: Steps are the held plateaus of the ramp; the settling seconds after each step up are excluded. Percentiles are request-weighted means of the per-second values, so compare them step to step rather than quoting them as an SLA. Capacity is the last step inside the SLO before throughput flattened; drive the follow-up performance test at the recommended level. Each step is judged by the profile's own thresholds: upper bounds on latency and errors decide whether the step held, while throughput or volume goals are measured and shown but never counted against a step — the first steps of a ramp are below them by design.
capacity.sloNone: No upper-bound threshold on this profile, so no step can be judged against an SLO — only the throughput curve is read. Add e.g. `p95 < 500` and `success_rate > 99` to get a capacity verdict.
capacity.notGating: a run-level goal — not counted against this step

config.title: Test profiles
config.requestsHint: Each step is one request per iteration, in order. Several steps let one virtual user walk several APIs, so the VU count stays the real concurrency of the run instead of splitting across parallel scenarios.
config.librdkafkaHint: Passed straight to librdkafka. Overrides every other producer setting.
config.maxMbHint: Volume test: stop once this much key + value data is sent.
config.latencyModeHint: End-to-end needs producer and consumer on one clock.
config.monitorLag: Chart consumer lag during the run
config.drainTimeoutSec: Wait for consumers to catch up (s, 0 = off)
config.drainTimeoutHint: After production stops, keep sampling until lag reaches 0 or this many seconds pass. Measures drain time.
config.thresholdHint: One per line, e.g. p95 < 500, success_rate > 99, rps > 1000
config.loadModelHint_vus: A fixed number of VUs for a fixed time — k6 vus/duration.
config.loadModelHint_stages: Ramp the VU count through a list of stages.
config.loadModelHint_rate: Fixed requests per second regardless of response time.
config.engineHint_ws: Plain WebSocket frames — no event names, no acknowledgements.
config.engineHint_socketio: Named events with optional acknowledgement callbacks. Connect over http:// or https://.
config.namespaceHint: Socket.IO namespace, e.g. /chat. Leave empty for the default.
config.transportsHint: Comma separated. Leave empty to let the client negotiate.
config.queryHint: Sent as query parameters on connect — often where a token goes.
config.scenariosHint: Each scenario is one journey. A virtual user runs exactly one of them, chosen by weight — so several scenarios split the same load instead of adding to it. They share the connection settings and phases above.
config.weightHint: Relative share of virtual users. Weights 3 and 1 mean 75% / 25%.
config.ackHint: Block until the server calls the acknowledgement callback, and time that round trip.
config.matchPathHint: Leave empty to accept any response. e.g. $.status
config.arrivalRateHint: New virtual users per second, held for the whole phase.
config.probeHint: Opens one connection, sends the flow's first message, and shows the reply.
config.thresholdDocForm: metric  operator  number      — one per line
config.thresholdDocExamples: Common thresholds — click one to add it:
config.thresholdDocInvalid: A line that names an unknown metric fails the run instead of being skipped, so a typo can never quietly pass.
config.thresholdDocK6: For REST profiles, latency, error-rate and rps thresholds are also given to k6 itself, so k6's own verdict agrees with the dashboard's. The rest are evaluated here.

thresholdMetric.p90: 90% of responses were faster than this
thresholdMetric.p95: 95% of responses were faster than this
thresholdMetric.p99: 99% of responses were faster than this
thresholdMetric.rps: Requests per second, averaged over the run
thresholdMetric.total_requests: Requests sent in the whole run
thresholdMetric.lag_max: Kafka: highest total consumer lag seen during the run
thresholdMetric.lag_avg: Kafka: mean consumer lag while load ran
thresholdMetric.lag_end: Kafka: consumer lag at the moment production stopped
thresholdMetric.lag_final: Kafka: consumer lag at the end of the run, after any drain wait
thresholdMetric.lag_growth: Kafka: lag added per second of load — above 0 means consumers fall behind
thresholdMetric.lag_drain_s: Kafka: seconds for consumers to reach lag 0 after production stopped (needs a drain wait; never caught up = fail)
thresholdMetric.total_mb: Kafka: data acknowledged in the whole run (key + value)
thresholdMetric.mb_per_s: Kafka: acknowledged MB per second over the load phase
thresholdMetric.msg_lag_avg: Kafka: mean time from produce to consumed (committed), per message — worst group
thresholdMetric.msg_lag_p50: Kafka: median per-message lag — worst group
thresholdMetric.msg_lag_p95: Kafka: 95% of messages were consumed within this — worst group
thresholdMetric.msg_lag_p99: Kafka: 99% of messages were consumed within this — worst group
thresholdMetric.msg_lag_max: Kafka: slowest message; any message left unconsumed fails it

config.rampHint: Replaces the stage list above with a stepped ramp. Hold each step long enough to measure it — a minute is a floor, several minutes is usual — then read the result in the run's capacity panel.
config.rampStartHint: First level. The ones after it are multiples of the step, so 1 + step 10 walks 1, 10, 20, 30 …

kafka.title: Kafka monitor
kafka.noGroups: No consumer group has committed offsets on these topics — there is no lag to report yet.
kafka.noLagYet: Collecting — the lag graph needs at least two samples.
kafka.noGroupMatch: No consumer group matches the current filter.
kafka.skipVerifyHint: Disables broker certificate checks. Use only against a test cluster.
kafka.authHint: Leave as PLAINTEXT for a local broker with no auth.
kafka.importAuthHint: Fill this form from a client.properties, YAML or JSON you already have.
kafka.importHint: Paste a librdkafka or Java client.properties, a KafkaJS options object, a Helm/YAML fragment, or KAFKA_* environment lines. Keys are matched however they are written — security.protocol, securityProtocol or KAFKA_SECURITY_PROTOCOL all land in the same field.
kafka.importPrivacy: The document is parsed, never executed, and is not saved — only the fields it fills are kept.
kafka.importBrokersHeld: brokers {{value}} not applied — stop the monitor first
kafka.clearAuthHint: Empty every authentication field and go back to PLAINTEXT.
kafka.clearedWhileRunning: Authentication cleared — the running monitor keeps its current settings until you stop and start it.

settings.title: Settings
settings.toolsHint: Runs a fixed install command on the machine hosting the dashboard. Recipes that need a root password cannot be run from here — copy them into a terminal instead.
settings.noMethod: No install recipe for this platform — see the tool documentation.

script.title: Import / Export
script.imported: Imported {{file}} as {{protocol}} — the form below is filled in
script.modeBuiltin: The script generated from the form below
script.modeInline: A script kept with this profile, run as written
script.modePath: An existing script file on this machine
script.inlinePlaceholder: Paste a k6 script here — it runs exactly as written, scenarios and all…
script.inlineHint: Saved with the profile and written to a temp file at run time, so it must be self-contained: relative imports and open() resolve against that directory. The form above is ignored. Multi-scenario scripts are fine — each scenario is reported separately.
script.envHint: Passed to k6 as --env (Artillery reads them from the process environment). Parameterise the target, rates and duration here instead of editing the script per run. CFG and SUMMARY_OUT are reserved.
script.runPastedHint: Run this script unchanged instead of mapping it onto the form
script.runPastedNote: The pasted script will run exactly as written — the form above is ignored.
script.pathHint: Executed where it lives, so relative imports, open() and CSV feeds keep working. The form below is ignored.
script.pastePlaceholder: Paste a k6 script, Artillery YAML or Kafka YAML here…
script.pasteHint: Parsed, never executed. If detection fails, pick the protocol in the dropdown and import again.
script.pickProtocol: pick the protocol in the dropdown and import again
